column1: # Lab capacity/identity table for the pre-push heavy-suite guard (OMN-16991).
# THIS FILE IS AUTHORITY FOR HOST IDENTITY. It is read from the COMMITTED tree
# (`git show HEAD:scripts/hooks/prepush_hosts.tsv`), never from the working
# tree, and the hook refuses if the two differ -- an uncommitted row whose
# `hostname` matches the local machine would otherwise self-designate a laptop
# as an authorizing gate host with no review, no receipt and no guard tripped.
# That is precisely the forgeable-on-disk-artifact surface OMN-16688
# deliberately avoided ("no file on disk to forge"). Adding or enabling a row
# therefore requires a reviewed commit, and tests/unit/scripts/
# test_prepush_host_table.py asserts the full contents so a row addition also
# requires a deliberate test update.
# Columns (TAB separated; no tabs inside any field):
#   label          stable row id; also names the per-row override env var
#                  PREPUSH_HOST_OVERRIDE_<LABEL uppercased>
#   role           capacity = placement candidate AND identity
#                  identity = identity only, never an execution target
#   hostname       `hostname -s` of that host, lowercased
#   ssh_target     ssh(1) target for probes/execution, or - for role=identity.
#                  A HOST, never a `user@host` (OMN-17280). ssh(1) resolves the
#                  login from ~/.ssh/config or the invoking account, so every
#                  actor reaches the lab as THEMSELVES. Before this column was
#                  a bare host it hardcoded one operator's login on every row,
#                  which meant a collaborator with his own account on `.201`
#                  could not reach a single execution target: measured
#                  2026-09-01, all four rows answered
#                  `Permission denied (publickey,password)` in under a second
#                  for a non-owner login, the ranked walk found nothing, and
#                  the push was refused. For the owner this is a no-op -- the
#                  account name the rows used to hardcode is the one ssh now
#                  resolves for him anyway. A login here is a DEFECT and
#                  test_no_capacity_row_hardcodes_an_ssh_login fails on it.
#   cores          nominal core count (documentation; the live probe re-reads it)
#   uv_abs_path    ABSOLUTE uv path. uv is on NO host's non-interactive PATH
#                  (measured 2026-08-29/30), so every remote leg invokes this
#                  path literally rather than relying on a login profile.
#   uv_min_version floor. A host below it is SKIPPED, never assumed fit -- the
#                  fleet spread is 0.8.3 -> 0.11.32 against uv.lock revision 3.
#   workroot       remote scratch root (bundles/, trees/, runs/, LOCK)
#   slot_mode      queue   = enqueue into ~/push-lanes/QUEUE (.201, OMN-16968)
#                  lockdir = exclusive mkdir(2) lockdir at <workroot>/LOCK
#                  none    = not an execution target
#   slots          (OMN-17269) how many CONCURRENT heavy-suite lanes this row
#                  may hold. Default 1 -- identical to the pre-OMN-17269 shape,
#                  one bare LOCK dir. slots=N gives the row N independently
#                  placeable candidates ("<label>" for slot 1, "<label>.<k>"
#                  for slot k>=2), each locked at <workroot>/LOCK for slot 1
#                  (unchanged path) and <workroot>/LOCK.<k> for slot k>=2, and
#                  each re-qualified on LIVE load at pick time -- a slot is
#                  never assumed fit merely because another slot on the same
#                  row is free.
#   repos_denied   comma-separated repos this host must NOT run, or -
#   mode           authorizing = its verdict may satisfy the escalation
#                  shadow      = runs and receipts, but NEVER authorizes
#                  disabled    = not probed, not run, not an identity
#   heavy_local    (OMN-17392) what happens when THIS row is the host doing the
#                  pushing. `allowed` = the pre-OMN-17392 behavior: if the local
#                  probe reads fit, run the heavy suite here. `prefer_remote` =
#                  attempt lab placement FIRST, and run here only after the
#                  bounded off-box wait is exhausted, with a loud notice. It is
#                  NOT a de-designation: a prefer_remote row keeps full identity
#                  and stays a placement target for every OTHER host. `-` on
#                  identity-only rows that never execute anything; as of
#                  OMN-17485 the gate-runner CONTAINER row (h201c) is an
#                  identity row that DOES execute (it is the local host of
#                  every in-container push), so it carries a real policy and
#                  prepush_heavy_local_policy reads identity rows too.
#   placement_tier (OMN-17485) how this row ranks as a PLACEMENT TARGET for
#                  heavy escalations. `default` = ranked by live load+memory
#                  exactly as before this column existed. `last_resort` = a
#                  legitimate, probed, verdict-bearing target that is chosen
#                  ONLY when no default-tier host is fit -- it can never
#                  outrank a fit default host, however idle it is. Used to
#                  keep hosts that carry live runtime-evidence lanes and
#                  interactive collaborator work (`.201`) from absorbing the
#                  lab's heavy suites by default, while still being reachable
#                  when the alternative is refusing the push. Operator-visible:
#                  the probe log tags the fit record `tier=last_resort`, and
#                  promotion back to `default` is a reviewed table edit plus a
#                  deliberate test update, the same two-step as a `mode`
#                  change. `-` on identity-only rows, which are never
#                  placement targets. Anything other than `last_resort` ranks
#                  as `default` -- the pre-OMN-17485 behavior.
#   note           free text
#label

column15: .200 Mac Studio; rule-11a default IDENTITY host. heavy_local=prefer_remote as of OMN-17392, operator directive 2026-08-31 verbatim "we should move prepush off this box if possible" -- this is the box. It stays authorizing and stays a placement target for every other host; what changed is that its OWN heavy escalations attempt lab placement first instead of running here the moment the local probe reads under 1.0x. Measured that day during landings: load1 96.58/24 = 4.02x, and a full-suite escalation was still eligible to run locally under the old rule because eligibility was only ever re-checked against the threshold, never against whether another host could take it. slots=1 -- widening this row is out of scope for OMN-17269 (it is the local/default host, not a distribution target)

.201 Linux host, 32 cores. OMN-16989 denial for omnibase_infra LIFTED: all 15 'host-coupled' failures were measured in the .201 gate-runner CONTAINER, not on this host over the remote leg. Re-measured 2026-08-30 over the real leg: tests/unit/ 24930 green in 669s, tests/ci/ 1892 green in 122s, both host_mode=authorizing pytest_exit=0. Separately PROVEN-CAPABLE for omnibase_core heavy escalations -- measured 2026-08-30 by parsing ~/push-lanes/queue-runner.log, not assumed: 12 completed heavy omnibase_core lanes span 2h43m20s (OMN-13902-main) to 3h48m55s (OMN-16581), 9 of them rc=0. So a core full suite costing ~10h on an M1 Air (OMN-16998) finishes here in under 4h. Reachable only by HAND-ROUTING a lane into that queue (~/push-lanes/lanes/<lane>.env + QUEUE): omnibase_core has no OMN-16991 dispatch seam of its own -- that gap is OMN-17159. slots=1 (OMN-17269) -- this row runs the separate ~/push-lanes/QUEUE serializer, a different concurrency mechanism; widening it is out of scope here OMN-17485: heavy_local flipped allowed -> prefer_remote and placement_tier set last_resort -- this host is the dev runtime lane's live evidence surface (the OMN-16963 AC5 delegation_workflow_state terminalization measurement reads from it) AND an interactive collaborator workspace (OMN-17143 lane), and on 2026-09-01 its gate-runner slot ran heavy suites back-to-back 08:31Z-12:02Z while a collaborator's own governed full core suite (44464 tests, 2h58m) ran host-side concurrently. A heavy escalation ORIGINATING here now attempts lab placement first (same OMN-17392 semantics as h200), and as a TARGET this row is taken only when no default-tier host is fit.

column15: .201 gate-runner CONTAINER hostname; no sshd (OMN-16446) so identity-only OMN-17485: carries heavy_local=prefer_remote because the container IS the local host of every in-container push and those escalations should look off-box first; with no ssh reachability from inside the container every probe refusal is structural, so the OMN-17392 ladder falls through to the same in-container slot path it used before -- strictly no wider.

OMN-17161: uv self-updated 0.8.3 -> 0.12.7 (2026-08-30), above the 0.11.0 floor. Re-probed non-interactively: load1 2.78/12 = 0.23x, ~89GB free on /System/Volumes/Data, /Users/Shared/onex-prepush confirmed writable (~/Code stays TCC-denied to sshd but is never used). Promoted straight to authorizing -- same reasoning as h105 (OMN-16991): a shadow row can never record a heavy verdict because the transplanted conftest.py refuses a full-suite target on any host outside the authorizing set, so the promotion is proven by a real full-suite dispatch instead, not a preceding shadow day. slots=1 -> 2 (OMN-17561): measured 2026-09-02~15:00Z load1 3.37/12 = 0.28x with exactly one full-suite pytest process running (omnibase_core, 1h42m elapsed, ~100% of one core) while six lanes queued for a placement host -- h105 (slots=2) unreachable over Tailscale/SSH, h200 at 1.9x, hcloud STOPPED. Widened to 2 slots on the same conservative doubling already proven on h105 (OMN-17269): slot 1 keeps the bare h101 label, slot 2 is h101.2, each re-qualified on live load/uv/busy state at pick time. Not widened past 2 -- no measurement yet of h101 carrying two concurrent full suites (peak memory/IO under real concurrent load); revisit upward only after that measurement.

MacBook Air M4, net-new capacity. Promoted shadow -> authorizing under the lab-wide distribution directive: probed fit 2026-08-30 (load1 1.76/10 = 0.18x, uv 0.11.8, 153 GB free) and its verdict must count, because a shadow row can never satisfy an escalation. slots=2 (OMN-17269): operator direction 2026-08-30 verbatim "it looks like .105 can take more load" -- re-measured same day: load1 2.74/10 = 0.27x, slot FREE, 10-core M4 with headroom for a second concurrent heavy-suite lane, re-qualified on live load at pick time for each slot independently

column15: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge i-02a5f8bc0833bdacd us-east-1a Elastic IP (OMN-16634) -- the cloud OVERFLOW/off-LAN target the operator ordered after the cloud leg was dropped twice (OMN-16523 R5 stranded, OMN-16634 canceled on an inferred rejection). Cannot displace lab-first placement: its default state is STOPPED (idle auto-stop, deploy/prepush-cloud/), a stopped host probes unreachable and is SKIPPED -- it competes only after a deliberate `aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-02a5f8bc0833bdacd` (~40s to reachable; EIP stable so this row never goes stale). Provisioned ONLY by the committed deploy/prepush-cloud/bootstrap.sh: git 2.43 + python 3.12.3 + uv 0.12.8 + shellcheck, NO docker (remote leg excludes tests/integration; unit+ci proven hermetic), NO tailnet (plain SSH, security group locked to lab+authorized egress IPs; platform-facing traffic goes through the gateway per unified-external-ingress), NO GitHub or AWS credentials on the host (bundle transport; idle-stop is an OS halt). Proven for omnibase_infra over the real bundle->scp->clone->uv sync->pytest transport 2026-09-01; the first governed full-suite escalation routed here is recorded on OMN-16634. Also the designated FIRST cloud target for the OMN-17226 per-host runner EFFECT. placement_tier=default DELIBERATELY, not last_resort (OMN-17485 column): lab-first is enforced by this row's LIFECYCLE -- its default state is STOPPED, so on an ordinary day the row is unreachable and the lab always wins. When an operator deliberately starts the box (lab saturated, off-LAN user), it must be able to take the work immediately, which default-tier load ranking gives it. last_resort exists to keep an ALWAYS-ON shared host (.201, live runtime-evidence lanes) from absorbing heavy suites; this host is nobody's runtime and costs money while up -- parking it last_resort would burn instance-hours waiting out fit lab hosts.
